1.say: You have never been up to the old village, have you? Only as far as the gorge. Then you have seen nothing. Above the gorge the road runs along a ridge for four kilometres, and on the north side there is a meadow that nobody has cut since I was a boy. Why not? With the bridge gone, there is no way to bring a cart up. So the grass grows and the copse at the top of it spreads about a metre a year. I should put that in the report. Put this in. The meeting over, we walked up there last summer, the four of us, and not one of us could find the old boundary. 'The meeting over, we walked up.' You have been listening to Kamola. I have been listening to Kamola for thirty years. It is a good sentence. The 'meeting' is its own subject; it is not us. Tired and half lost, we came down in the dark. Put that in too and see whether the ministry cares. They will not. But the district will, and they are the ones who have to vote.

grammar.label: absolute constructions — with and without 'with'
grammar.form: (With +) noun phrase + participle / adjective / prepositional phrase, then the main clause
grammar.meaning: attaches a circumstance to a clause without a conjunction

explanation.en: 'The meeting over, we walked back.' 'With the bridge closed, the school opened late.' The absolute has its own subject, different from the main clause's, and no finite verb. Without 'with' it is literary; with 'with' it is ordinary formal English. The error is to give it the same subject as the main clause, which makes a dangling participle instead.
explanation.uz: 'The meeting over, we walked back.' Absolyut qurilmaning O'Z egasi bor va u bosh gap egasidan farq qiladi; shaxsli fe'l yo'q. Xato — bir xil ega qo'yish: u holda 'dangling participle' hosil bo'ladi.

grammar.positive_example: With the road still under water, the inspection was postponed.
grammar.negative_example: Still under water, the inspection was postponed.

l1_notes.uz: Bu tuzilma o'zbek tilida -gach, -ib, -gan holda bilan beriladi; ingliz tilida ega aniq ko'rsatilishi shart.

grammar.label: verbless and supplementive clauses
grammar.form: adjective phrase / noun phrase set off by commas, sharing the main subject
grammar.meaning: adds a second predication without a second sentence

explanation.en: 'Tired and hungry, they walked the last mile.' 'A lawyer by training, she read the clause twice.' These share the main clause's subject and have no verb at all. They differ from absolutes precisely there: the absolute has its own subject, the supplementive borrows one. Put the wrong subject next to it and the sentence says something absurd.
explanation.uz: 'Tired and hungry, they walked the last mile.' Bu qurilma bosh gap egasini O'ZIGA oladi va fe'li yo'q. Absolyutdan farqi shu: absolyutning o'z egasi bor, bunisi esa qarzga oladi.

grammar.positive_example: A teacher for thirty years, Kamola knew every family in the village.
grammar.negative_example: A teacher for thirty years, the village was familiar to Kamola.

l1_notes.uz: Xato deyarli har doim egani almashtirishdan kelib chiqadi; o'zbek tilida ega tushirilishi mumkin, ingliz tilida esa bu ma'noni buzadi.

story.title: With the road still under water

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: You have never been up to the old village, have you?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Only as far as the gorge.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Then you have seen nothing. Above the gorge the road runs along a ridge for four kilometres, and on the north side there is a meadow that nobody has cut since I was a boy.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: With the bridge gone, there is no way to bring a cart up. So the grass grows and the copse at the top of it spreads about a metre a year.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I should put that in the report.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Put this in. The meeting over, we walked up there last summer, the four of us, and not one of us could find the old boundary.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The meeting over, we walked up.' You have been listening to Kamola.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: I have been listening to Kamola for thirty years.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It is a good sentence. The 'meeting' is its own subject; it is not us.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Tired and half lost, we came down in the dark. Put that in too and see whether the ministry cares.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: They will not. But the district will, and they are the ones who have to vote.
